title: READ-001: Standardize function definition patterns
description: API functions use inconsistent patterns. The login() function uses direct fetch instead of the request() helper, breaking the pattern used by logout() and other API functions. Standardizing all functions to use the request() helper improves consistency and maintainability.

context.inconsistency: login() uses direct fetch; logout() and others use request() helper
context.goal: All API functions should use request() helper for consistency

acceptance_criteria: login() function uses request() helper like logout()
All API functions (getUsers, createUser, deleteUser, etc.) follow same pattern
Error handling remains consistent across all functions
login() signature and return type unchanged (backwards compatible)
No behavioral changes; only structural refactoring

implementation_notes.note: request() helper handles fetch call and auth headers; validateResponse() still applies schema validation

unit_test: Test login() with valid credentials returns LoginResponse
Test login() with invalid credentials returns error
Verify request() helper is called with correct method and path
integration_test: Test login endpoint still works after refactoring
Verify error handling (network error, invalid response) still works
Test response schema validation catches invalid responses
manual_test: Login with valid credentials in dashboard
Verify login succeeds and token is stored
Check browser DevTools Network tab for POST /api/auth/login request
Try invalid credentials and verify error message appears

rollback_plan: git revert <commit-hash> — isolated change to login() function
notes: This is a structural refactoring improving consistency. No behavioral changes; only moves login() to use same request() helper pattern as other API functions.
